title: What a shopper's browser gets
grade_reasons: C stands. The base is sound and partly held: 447 KB of a store page's 680 to 778 KB of first scripts is React and Next, a default store loads no third-party script and no font file, the extras are lazy, and two script budgets and an import scan exist. But every view sends the layout twice, makes one or two server calls for nothing and 11 to 47 router requests with 33 to 205 KB of scripts for pages nobody asked for, and eleven working routes share a bundle 98 KB too large. The budgets cover 2 of 58 store routes with 14 to 16% of room, and no themed store, filled cart, checkout or time on a phone was ever measured.
verdict_on_bar: Kept: the floor is real. I measured it on the build: seven files, 447,102 bytes raw (133,758 gzip, 114,997 Brotli), in the first-load list of all 560 routes; the leanest page route is 479,303. On that floor 615,000 for a built page, 650,000 for a listing, 135,000 for the stylesheet, a home document of 112,000 with nothing twice, 0 calls of the page's own, 6 router requests on a phone, the press costs and Lighthouse 90 are what a strict engineer would ask. Tightened, because the steward's own sums go further: product page 690,000 to 670,000 (690,000 is the figure with four pickers a plain product never draws still loaded); cart and checkout 700,000 to 670,000 and account 700,000 to 650,000 (700,000 passes with 30 to 70 KB of other routes' parts still on board); /products 150,000 to 120,000 (the layout fix alone reaches 140,674, so 150,000 tests nothing); a recommending grid 335,000 to 140,000 (335,000 still holds zod and the page model). Added: what a visit weighs in all, and the scripts fetched after the page's own (33 to 205 KB raw per page today, seen by no check, and the way the 19 KB of 10 November got in); a bar at 1280 px, since the steward's was phone only; no request to another host, held; and the themed store and the money path must meet the bars, not only be recorded at a first figure. The two after-load measures are merged into one to make room. Loosened: no number, but two tolerances are now named. The filter's button stays in first scripts and only its panel loads late, and a product picker stays if a press test shows it must (25,423 bytes at most): the written rule says a press before a part's script runs is lost, and step 0.16 as written breaks it. Not measurable as written: font bytes in CI are stand-in files, so they are read in production each night; the field figure needs 20 page loads; the duplicate-row and client-module counters (flight.mjs, route.mjs) are not among the seven scripts in the repo and step 0.1 does not name them.

measures.name: First scripts of a first visit, by route, and the stylesheet
measures.today: Raw bytes of the script tags in the server's HTML, nomodule left out: built page 680,264 (213,261 gzip); product page 777,785; category, search, cart, checkout, account and six more 778,166. Of each, 447,102 (133,758 gzip) is React, Next and Turbopack's runtime, the same seven files on all 560 routes. A recommending grid adds 649,561 after its answer. One stylesheet for stores, site and admin: 183,124 raw, 25,832 Brotli.
measures.target_a: Built page at most 615,000 (about 192 KB gzip; 168 KB over the framework). Listing and search at most 650,000. A plain product page at most 670,000. Cart and checkout at most 670,000. Account, wishlist, order and cookies at most 650,000. A recommending grid at most 140,000 after its answer, with no zod, page model or whole language. The storefront's own stylesheet at most 135,000 raw and 20,600 Brotli.
measures.how_measured: FIRST_SCRIPTS_BUDGETS in e2e/performance.spec.ts, once step 1.3 counts the server's script tags without the nomodule file (8 store routes, within 3%). scripts/bundle-budget.mjs of step 1.2 for all 560 routes. e2e/recommendations.spec.ts (step 2.10). The stylesheet budget of step 1.3, lowered by step 2.11.

measures.name: The store document: its size, what is in it twice, and whether a function draws it
measures.today: Home 138,523 bytes raw (18,691 gzip); 106.7 to 170.3 thousand over 12 pages; 66 to 71% is the inline payload. The layout is in every document twice (35 rows, 29,655 bytes raw). /products sends its 9 products twice (24.7 KB). A store in an AI-translated language would add about 93 KB of texts, of which the browser reads 114 of 1,673. 148 of 149 prerendered store routes are drawn by a function on each view.
measures.target_a: Nothing twice: one html element in the payload and under 2,000 bytes of duplicate rows; each fixed style sheet twice per document (once in the HTML, once in the payload) whatever the number of rows. Home at most 112,000 raw. /om-oss at most 85,000. /products at most 120,000, each product once. The texts of a translated language under 9,000 bytes. Home, built and blog pages are static files.
measures.how_measured: DOCUMENT_BUDGETS in e2e/performance.spec.ts (step 1.3: 5 routes within 5%), with the html-element and duplicate-row counts that step 2.2 adds. e2e/listing.spec.ts (step 2.12). The test of uiTextsFor() (step 0.8). scripts/render-modes.baseline.json (steps 1.11 and 2.4).

measures.name: What a page asks for after it has loaded, for a visitor who presses nothing
measures.today: Router requests on a phone: home 11 at the top and 47 read to the footer (204 KB on the wire), 24 of them for other language, currency and country views; content page 34; empty cart 42; a multi-country front door 12. At 1440 px the home makes 17 at the top. A full listing of 48 tiles: not measured, about 96 by multiplication. Calls of the page's own: 1 or 2 on all 12 pages (wishlist, tile stock, a search suggestion). Scripts beyond the HTML's own: 3 to 10 files and 33 to 205 KB raw per store page; 12 files and 511 KB on Kaizena Flow's home. On a local build 9 of 11 store pages never go quiet.
measures.target_a: Router requests: at most 6 on a phone on the home, a product page, a content page and the cart, at the top and read to the footer; at most 8 at the top at 1280 px; 0 for another view, for a link that leaves its root layout and for /admin; at most 20 on a seeded 48-tile listing read to the end; none between 3 and 5 s after load. Calls of the page's own: 0 on all 12 pages. Late scripts: at most 2 files and 30,000 bytes raw on a phone (the cart drawer's), and none of the admin's on Kaizena Flow's pages. Requests to another host: 0 on a default store.
measures.how_measured: e2e/prefetch.spec.ts, made by steps 0.12 and 0.14, with one table of budgets from step 1.3. The after-load fetch count in e2e/performance.spec.ts and the assertions of step 0.15 in e2e/wishlist.spec.ts, e2e/shop-components.spec.ts and e2e/search.spec.ts. measure-routes.mjs for the full table. The 1280 px row, the late-script count and the other-host count are in no step's done-when yet: see shortfalls.

measures.name: Everything a cold phone visit downloads before the page is idle
measures.today: On the wire with gzip, at the top of the page: home 406,542 bytes in 48 requests; product page 423,097; content page 550,705 in 70; empty cart 591,352 in 78. Held at 450,000 on two pages, counted until two seconds after load.
measures.target_a: At most 350,000 bytes on the home, a product page, a listing, a content page and the cart of the bare store (the sums give about 323,000 to 335,000). Each themed page within 4% of its figure after phase 2.
measures.how_measured: SPEED_BUDGETS in e2e/performance.spec.ts, widened from 2 pages to 5 and counted until the network has been quiet for three seconds, as measure-routes.mjs does. Finding SC-6 step 4 wrote this; step 1.3's done-when leaves it out, so a shortfall step adds it.

measures.name: What a press costs
measures.today: A product tile on a built page: a whole document, 42 requests, 104.5 KB on the wire (a link inside the app: 5 requests, 12.9 KB). The cart on a screen of 768 px or more: the drawer is fetched ahead (3 requests and 2 script chunks), drawn, thrown away, and the page loaded. The first Add to cart: an answer of 79,467 bytes with the layout twice, then 32 router events, 20 of them on the network.
measures.target_a: Tile press: 0 documents and at most 8 requests. Cart press at 1280 px: 1 document, 0 router requests, and nothing fetched ahead for it. First Add to cart: 1 request, an answer under 5,000 bytes, no redraw of the page, then at most 10 router events.
measures.how_measured: Cases in e2e/prefetch.spec.ts (steps 2.6 and 2.7) and in e2e/cart.spec.ts (steps 2.2 and 2.4).

measures.name: The pages real shoppers get: a themed store and the money path
measures.today: Not measured. All 12 measured store pages are the bare template: 0 font files, one-row pages, pictures of about 1 KB. Each of the six launch themes names two font families. The cart was measured empty, and the checkout load ended on the cart. Production's demo home is 203 KB raw against 138 KB locally.
measures.target_a: A launch-theme store's home, product page, listing and a built page, a cart with two lines and the checkout at its payment step are in the measured set, and meet the bars above for requests, calls, duplicates and late scripts. Themed home: at most 2 font files and 80 KB before the largest paint, both preloaded; no picture drawn from a file with more than twice the pixels its box needs on a 3x phone. Checkout at its payment step: first scripts at most 670,000, 0 router requests while the form shows, and the payment provider's script the only request to another host.
measures.how_measured: Steps 1.6 and 1.7 create it: a seeded Orbit store and a payments stand-in in CI, added to measure-routes.mjs and e2e/performance.spec.ts. Font bytes are read in production by the nightly run of step 1.14, because CI's font files are stand-ins.

measures.name: Time on a slow phone
measures.today: Not measured for a store and not held. Lighthouse runs by hand. kaizenaflow.com, the one themed page measured, scored 83 to 88 on a phone on 5 November with its largest paint at 3.7 to 4.3 s. The bare demo store scored 92 to 96 on a local build. Real visitors' figures exist only where an owner switched visit counting on, and never for cart or checkout.
measures.target_a: Each night in production, phone form, the median of three runs: performance 90 or more and blocking time at most 200 ms, on the launch-theme store's home, product page and listing and on Kaizena Flow's front page. In CI: script bytes run by idle held within 5% on four pages. In the field: Kaizena Flow's demo stores count visits, and with 20 page loads or more the 75th percentile is inside the product's own 'good' lines (largest paint 2.5 s, response to a press 200 ms, layout shift 0.1).
measures.how_measured: Step 1.14 creates it: a nightly workflow beside .github/workflows/live-a11y.yml that runs scripts/perf.mjs --form=mobile --min=90, a throttled run in measure-routes.mjs, a run-bytes budget in e2e/performance.spec.ts, and commerce.speed_samples for the field figure. Its nightly run names two pages; the product page and the listing must be added.

measures.name: What holds it
measures.today: First scripts are held on 2 of 58 store routes, with 14 to 16% of room and a legacy file counted in. Weight is held on 2 pages with 6 to 10% of room. Nothing holds a document, a request count, a late script, an action's answer or a time. 4 of 947 links state a prefetch policy. Two additions of 10 and 11 November (19 KB on every product page; a server call and 19 KB of lazy script on every product grid) passed every check.
measures.target_a: Every store route's first scripts held by the all-routes check, and 8 of them in the browser within 3%. Documents on 5 routes within 5%. Weight on 5 pages within 4%. Router requests on 6 pages at the measured count plus 2, one of them at 1280 px. Late script files held exactly. next/link imported only by the policy wrappers, by a ratchet that only falls. The storefront's import scan follows import(). The nightly time check fails when red two nights running. A budget is lowered in the change that lowers its measure.
measures.how_measured: e2e/performance.spec.ts, e2e/prefetch.spec.ts, e2e/cart.spec.ts, scripts/bundle-budget.mjs, src/server/ratchet.scan.test.ts (directLinks), src/lib/storefront-bundle.scan.test.ts and the nightly workflow. Steps 1.2, 1.3, 1.14, 2.6 and 2.10 make them; weight, late scripts and the 1280 px row are the shortfall step.

bar_in_a_sentence: A shopper's first page loads React and Next plus at most 168 KB of the store's own script on a built page (203 to 223 KB where it sells or pays), one document with nothing in it twice, and no more than 350 KB on the wire in all; left alone it fetches at most 6 answers ahead and calls the server for nothing. A themed store in production scores 90 on a slow phone every night, and a check fails on the day any of this slips.
can_the_steps_reach_a: No, not as written. The bytes and counts get there. Built page 680,264 to 611,249 (step 0.16). Product page 777,785 to 664,471 with the pickers split, 689,894 without. Listing 778,166 to between 623,000 and 644,000, cart to about 653,000 (steps 0.16 and 2.9). Stylesheet 183,124 to 129,745 (2.11). Home document 138,523 to 108,868, /products 170,329 to 115,974 (2.2, 2.12). Phone home read to the footer: 47 router requests to 23 (0.12) to 3 (2.6). Calls of the page's own to 0 (0.15). A tile press from 42 requests to at most 8 (2.7). The Add to cart answer from 79,467 bytes to under 5,000 (2.4). A visit's weight from 406,542 to about 323,000. Three things stop short. Time: the one themed page measured scored 83 to 88 against a bar of 90, the cuts take about 26 KB compressed off some 400 KB its largest paint waits for, and no step is aimed at that. Holds: no done-when holds a visit's weight, late scripts or a wide screen, so those can slip back unseen. Done-whens: four pass 20 to 195 KB short of the bar (steps 0.16, 2.9, 2.10, 2.12) and step 2.2 lacks one check. The listing's 20 also waits for the owner's yes in step 2.8. Three steps are added to the plan's ladder because the bar needs them: 0.1 and 1.11 make two of its checks, and 2.3 draws each style sheet once. Steps 2.27 and 2.34 are on the plan's ladder for this area but move the owner's browser and no measure here, so they are left out. With the five changes under shortfalls the area is an A once phase 2's cuts are in and the nightly figures have been green for a week.

shortfalls.what: Time. Lighthouse 90 on a themed page is not shown to be reachable. kaizenaflow.com scored 83 to 88 on a phone with its largest paint at 3.7 to 4.3 s (3.75 s after its fonts were cut to 67 KB); by Lighthouse's weights a score of 90 needs roughly 3.3 to 3.5 s. The plan's cuts are about 20 KB gzip of script and 6 KB of stylesheet. Short by 2 to 7 points. Step 1.14 also sits in phase 1 with a done-when (a green week) that only phase 2 can earn, and its nightly run names the store's home and Kaizena Flow's front page, not the product page and listing.
shortfalls.proposed_step_title: Cut what the largest paint waits for on a themed page
shortfalls.proposed_step_what: Phase 2, effort M. When step 1.14 has a week of figures, repeat the test of 5 November on the launch-theme store's home, product page and listing in production: block the fonts, the scripts and the stylesheet in turn and write down the largest paint each time. Then cut what the table names until the line holds. The evidence so far points at fonts: without them the same page scored 93. Preload only the family the first screen draws, cut each family's file to the letters the store's languages use, and keep the cart drawer's prefetch out of the first three seconds. Change step 1.14's done-when to 'has run for a week and its figures are in docs/performance.md', and add the product page and the listing to its run.
shortfalls.proposed_done_when: The nightly job shows a median of 90 or more and blocking time of 200 ms or less on the launch-theme store's home, product page and listing and on Kaizena Flow's front page for seven nights in a row; the blocking table is in docs/performance.md; and font bytes before the largest paint are a budget in the nightly file.

shortfalls.what: Holds. Nothing holds the scripts a page fetches after its own (33 to 205 KB raw per store page today, 511 KB on Kaizena Flow's home), the weight of a whole visit, requests to another host, or requests on a wide screen. Step 1.3 closes SC-6 but its done-when leaves out SC-6's weight budget. Step 2.6's done-when has no 1280 px case and no sub-menu case, though PF-3 and PF-8 wrote both. The 19 KB lazy chunk of 10 November would pass again.
shortfalls.proposed_step_title: Hold the whole visit: weight, late scripts, other hosts and a wide screen
shortfalls.proposed_step_what: Phase 1, effort S, as part of step 1.3. In e2e/performance.spec.ts count for the home, a product page, a listing, a content page and the cart on a phone, from a cold cache until the network has been quiet for three seconds: bytes on the wire, script files beyond the HTML's own tags with their raw bytes, and requests to another host. Set weight at its figure plus 4%, and the two counts exactly. In e2e/prefetch.spec.ts add the store home at 1280 px and a header menu with sub-links. Each later step lowers its own figures. Copy the review's flight.mjs and route.mjs into the repo with step 0.1: steps 2.2 and 2.9 are proved with them.
shortfalls.proposed_done_when: The spec holds five pages' weight within 4%, their late script files and bytes, and 0 requests to another host. After phase 2 each page is at or under 350,000 bytes on the wire with at most 2 late script files of 30,000 bytes raw together. e2e/prefetch.spec.ts holds the home at 1280 px at 8 router requests or fewer and 0 for a sub-link before its top link is hovered. A branch that adds a 15 KB lazy chunk to a product grid fails.

shortfalls.what: Done-whens weaker than the bar. Step 0.16 passes the product page at 690,000, the figure with the pickers still loaded (664,471 with them split). Step 2.9 passes cart, checkout and account at 700,000, which still has room for 30 to 70 KB of other routes' parts (about 653,000 and 627,000 by the module sizes). Step 2.12 passes /products under 150,000, which step 2.2 alone reaches (140,674; both give 115,974). Step 2.10 passes a recommending grid at 335,000, a figure that still holds the zod and page model its own text forbids (about 139,000 without). Step 2.2 does not check that nothing is fetched ahead for the cart on a wide screen.
shortfalls.proposed_step_title: Set five done-whens at what the sums reach
shortfalls.proposed_step_what: No new work, only the figures. Step 0.16: a plain product page at most 670,000. Step 2.9: cart and checkout at most 670,000; account, wishlist, order and cookies at most 650,000. Step 2.12: /products at most 120,000. Step 2.10: at most 140,000 after the answer. Step 2.2: 0 router requests for the cart before the press at 1280 px (3 today, with 2 script chunks).
shortfalls.proposed_done_when: The plan's text holds these five figures, and the budgets of steps 1.2 and 1.3 are lowered to them in the changes that reach them.

shortfalls.what: The press rule. Step 0.16 loads the listing's filter dialog and the product's pickers late. The written rule (docs/performance.md lines 44 to 49, and the comment at the top of src/components/lazy/blocks.tsx) keeps exactly these in first scripts, because a press before a part's own script runs was lost. One audit left them for that reason; another moved them. The built page's 615,000 needs the dialog out: with it the page is 623,022, which is 8 KB over.
shortfalls.proposed_step_title: Keep the filter's button, load its panel on the first press, and let a press test decide the pickers
shortfalls.proposed_step_what: Part of step 0.16. Split src/components/filter-dialog.tsx (500 lines, one component) into the button, which stays in first scripts, and the panel, loaded on the first press or when a pointer nears. Load the four pickers through lazy stand-ins only if the bookings, gift card, quote, gallery and custom-fields-ranges specs pass five times each on Chromium and WebKit. A picker that loses a press stays, and docs/performance.md names it with its bytes as tolerance. Correct the rule's text either way.
shortfalls.proposed_done_when: The home's first scripts are at most 615,000 and none holds 'filter-dialog-title'; the filter opens on a first press in e2e/custom-fields-ranges.spec.ts five runs in five on both engines; and docs/performance.md lists each part that stays in first scripts with its bytes.

shortfalls.what: Real pages are recorded, not judged. Steps 1.6 and 1.7 hold the themed store and the money path within 5% of a first figure taken before phase 2. Only fonts and the checkout's requests have a number to meet, and the font figure comes from stand-in files in CI.
shortfalls.proposed_step_title: Read the themed store and the money path against the bar
shortfalls.proposed_step_what: Part of steps 1.6 and 1.7, finished after phase 2. The themed home, product page, listing and built page and the two-line cart meet the same bars as the bare store for router requests, calls of the page's own, duplicate rows and late scripts. The checkout at its payment step has first scripts of at most 670,000. No picture on the themed home is drawn from a file with more than twice the pixels its box needs on a 3x phone. Font files and bytes are read from the production demo store by the nightly run.
shortfalls.proposed_done_when: e2e/performance.spec.ts and e2e/prefetch.spec.ts hold those figures for the six pages, the nightly file shows at most 2 font files and 80 KB before the largest paint on the themed home, and the table of step 4.5 lists each themed and money-path figure beside its bar.

tolerated: The framework: 447 KB raw (134 KB gzip) of React and Next on every page. Nothing here can remove it.
The browser's words in all four languages together: 24.8 KB raw, about 7 KB gzip. Loading one language made presses get lost (D212).
The site form and the carousel in every built page's first scripts, 13 to 20 KB raw, because a visitor may press them before a late script would arrive.
The staff links and five small parts (two beacons, the footer guard, two A/B parts) on every page: about 10 KB raw.
The filter's button on every built page, and any product picker that a press test shows cannot load late: up to 25 KB raw on a product page, each named with its bytes.
The payload: the page again as data, about twice its markup. The router needs it to wake the page and to move without a reload.
On a phone the cart link is fetched on sight (3 requests), and so is the first screen of a listing's tiles, within the bound of 20.
After the first Add to cart the router asks again for the links on sight, about 7 events. That is Next's behaviour when a cookie is set.
Cart on a wide screen and checkout open by a full page load. That is the pay-route rule, not waste.
The default icon: 26 KB raw, about 9 KB on the wire, once per site, at low priority (PL-12).
motion.css in the stylesheet: 18.7 KB raw, 3.8 KB Brotli, also for a store with no motion (CS-2).
Lighthouse scores move a few points between runs, so the nightly check takes the median of three and fails only on two nights in a row.
owner_choices: On a full listing, may only the first screen of product tiles be fetched ahead on sight and the rest when touched (or all through one shared shell, if the trial in step 2.8 shows that works)? Today every tile seen is fetched: about 96 requests for 48 products, of which a shopper opens one or two. Without a yes the listing has no bound and the area stays a B.

On a computer, may the main menu's links wait for the pointer before their pages are fetched? Then a wide screen fetches nothing at rest. Kept on sight, each top link costs 2 requests on every page view, and the 1280 px bar of 8 only fits a menu of three links. The trial in step 2.8 can give the number first.

After the stylesheet split (step 2.11), a Tailwind class typed in a part's Advanced tab can show on the builder's canvas and not on the live site. Is it enough to say in the docs that only classes styled by the owner's own CSS are promised, or should the site's sheet keep a short fixed list of utility names owners may type?
